questions.knowledgeNote: Antiderivative = any function whose derivative returns the given function; the +c family is the whole answer set of an indefinite integral.
questions.question: AQ1. What is an antiderivative? Is it true that there are a number of antiderivatives of a function which differ from one another only by a constant? Show this relation by taking an example.
questions.solution: An antiderivative (primitive) of f on an interval is a function F with F'(x) = f(x) for every x in the interval. Yes, the statement is true: if F is one antiderivative then F + c is another for every constant c, and conversely any two antiderivatives of the same f on an interval differ by a constant - because (F - G)' = f - f = 0, and a function with zero derivative on an interval is constant (mean value theorem). Example: for f(x) = 3x^2, the functions x^3, x^3 + 5, x^3 - 7 and in general x^3 + c all differentiate to 3x^2, and any two of them differ only by a constant. That is exactly why the indefinite integral is written integral 3x^2 dx = x^3 + c. Boxed (printed book p605, theory).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ1; book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Indefinite integral = a family of functions (the antiderivatives); definite integral = one number, the signed area, and the two are linked by the fundamental theorem.
questions.question: AQ2. What does an indefinite integral mean? How does it differ from a definite integral? What does integral from a to b of f(x) dx represent?
questions.solution: The indefinite integral integral f(x) dx denotes the whole family of antiderivatives of f, i.e. F(x) + c where F' = f; its value is a function (plus an arbitrary constant). The definite integral integral from a to b of f(x) dx is a single real number computed as F(b) - F(a) for any antiderivative F; the arbitrary constant cancels, so the answer does not depend on which antiderivative is chosen. Geometrically, integral from a to b of f(x) dx represents the signed area between the graph of y = f(x), the x-axis, and the vertical lines x = a and x = b: area above the axis counts positive, area below counts negative, and the two cancel where the curve changes sign. The link between the two notions is the fundamental theorem of calculus: d/dx integral from a to x of f(t) dt = f(x). Boxed (printed book p605, theory).

questions.knowledgeNote: Expand the cube with the binomial theorem, then integrate term by term; the x^(-2) term is the only one needing the power rule with a negative exponent.
questions.question: AQ3(i). Evaluate: integral of (x + 1/x)^3 dx.
questions.solution: Expand: (x + 1/x)^3 = x^3 + 3x + 3/x + 1/x^3. Integrate term by term: x^4/4 + 3x^2/2 + 3 log|x| + x^(-2)/(-2) + c = x^4/4 + 3x^2/2 + 3 log x - 1/(2x^2) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute u = 6x + 8 and rewrite the linear factor 2x + 3 in terms of u: it becomes (u + 1)/3.
questions.question: AQ3(ii). Evaluate: integral of (2x + 3)(6x + 8)^5 dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 6x + 8, so x = (u - 8)/6, dx = du/6 and 2x + 3 = (u - 8)/3 + 3 = (u + 1)/3. The integral becomes (1/18) integral (u + 1) u^5 du = (1/18)(u^7/7 + u^6/6) = u^6(6u + 7)/756. Back-substituting 6u + 7 = 6(6x + 8) + 7 = 36x + 55 gives (1/756)(36x + 55)(6x + 8)^6 + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor both differences with the sum-to-product formulas; nearly everything cancels and 2(cos x + cos alpha) is left.
questions.question: AQ3(iv). Evaluate: integral of (cos 2x - cos 2alpha)/(cos x - cos alpha) dx.
questions.solution: cos 2x - cos 2alpha = -2 sin(x + alpha) sin(x - alpha) and cos x - cos alpha = -2 sin((x+alpha)/2) sin((x-alpha)/2). The ratio is [2 sin(x+alpha) sin(x-alpha)]/[2 sin((x+alpha)/2) sin((x-alpha)/2)] = 4 cos((x+alpha)/2) cos((x-alpha)/2) = 2(cos x + cos alpha), using sin 2t = 2 sin t cos t twice and 2 cos A cos B = cos(A+B) + cos(A-B). Hence the integral = 2(sin x + x cos alpha) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Both lines collapse by sum-to-product: the numerator is 2 sin x sin alpha and the denominator 2 sin x cos alpha.
questions.question: AQ3(v). Evaluate: integral of [cos(x - alpha) - cos(x + alpha)]/[sin(x + alpha) + sin(x - alpha)] dx.
questions.solution: cos(x - alpha) - cos(x + alpha) = 2 sin x sin alpha and sin(x + alpha) + sin(x - alpha) = 2 sin x cos alpha. The quotient is therefore tan alpha - a constant - so the integral is x tan alpha + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: The numerator is a difference of squares: e^(2x) - 1 = (e^x - 1)(e^x + 1), so the fraction cancels to e^x - 1.
questions.question: AQ3(vi). Evaluate: integral of (e^(2x) - 1)/(e^x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: (e^(2x) - 1)/(e^x + 1) = (e^x - 1)(e^x + 1)/(e^x + 1) = e^x - 1. Hence the integral = e^x - x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(vi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by (sec x - tan x) so the denominator becomes sec^2 - tan^2 = 1; the result is 1/(1 + sin x) = sec^2 x - sec x tan x.
questions.question: AQ3(vii). Evaluate: integral of sec x/(sec x + tan x) dx.
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (sec x - tan x): sec x(sec x - tan x)/(sec^2 x - tan^2 x) = sec^2 x - sec x tan x. Both terms are immediate derivatives: integral = tan x - sec x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ3(vii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Split the fraction term by term: sin^3/(sin^2 cos^2) = sin/cos^2 = sec x tan x, and cos^3/(sin^2 cos^2) = cos/sin^2 = -d(cosec x)/dx.
questions.question: AQ3(viii). Evaluate: integral of (a sin^3 x + b cos^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) dx.
questions.solution: (a sin^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) = a sin x/cos^2 x = a sec x tan x, whose integral is a sec x. (b cos^3 x)/(sin^2 x cos^2 x) = b cos x/sin^2 x, whose integral is -b cosec x. Hence the answer is a sec x - b cosec x + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Put u = sqrt(3x + 1) (so x = (u^2 - 1)/3) - the square root disappears and a plain polynomial in u remains.
questions.question: AQ4(i). Evaluate: integral of (2x + 3)/sqrt(3x + 1) dx. (T.U. 2048).
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt(3x + 1); then 3x + 1 = u^2, x = (u^2 - 1)/3, dx = 2u du/3 and 2x + 3 = (2u^2 + 7)/3. The integral = integral [(2u^2 + 7)/3](2u du/3)/u = (2/9) integral (2u^2 + 7) du = (2/9)(2u^3/3 + 7u) = (2/27) u (2u^2 + 21). Since 2u^2 + 21 = 2(3x + 1) + 21 = 6x + 23, the answer is (2/27)(6x + 23) sqrt(3x + 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.question: AQ4(v). Evaluate: integral of tan^3 x sec^4 x dx. (T.U. 2051).
questions.solution: Let u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx and sec^4 x = (1 + u^2)^2. The integral = integral u^3 (1 + u^2) du = u^4/4 + u^6/6 + c = tan^4 x/4 + tan^6 x/6 + c. Boxed (printed key p607).

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalise the denominator: the product of the conjugates is the constant a + b, which pulls out of the integral.
questions.question: AQ4(viii). Evaluate: integral of dx/[sqrt(3x + a) - sqrt(3x - b)]. (HSEB 2050).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (sqrt(3x+a) + sqrt(3x-b)): the denominator becomes (3x + a) - (3x - b) = a + b, a constant. So the integral = (1/(a+b)) integral [sqrt(3x + a) + sqrt(3x - b)] dx = (1/(a+b))[(2/9)(3x + a)^(3/2) + (2/9)(3x - b)^(3/2)] + c = (2/(9(a+b)))[(3x + a)^(3/2) + (3x - b)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: The numerator is exactly d(x + cos x)/dx: a logarithmic form hiding in plain sight.
questions.question: AQ5(i). Evaluate: integral of (1 - sin x)/(x + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: d/dx (x + cos x) = 1 - sin x, so with u = x + cos x the integral is integral du/u = log|x + cos x| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so the answer is a single logarithm (this is the integral of tanh x).
questions.question: AQ5(ii). Evaluate: integral of (e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)) dx.
questions.solution: d/dx (e^x + e^(-x)) = e^x - e^(-x), so the integral = log(e^x + e^(-x)) + c (the quantity is positive, so no modulus is needed). Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(ii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: d(x e^x) = e^x(1 + x) dx, so the integrand is sec^2 u du with u = x e^x.
questions.question: AQ5(iii). Evaluate: integral of e^x (1 + x)/cos^2(x e^x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x e^x; then du = (e^x + x e^x) dx = e^x(1 + x) dx. The integral = integral sec^2 u du = tan u + c = tan(x e^x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(iii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Note (x + 1)/x = 1 + 1/x = d(x + log x)/dx: the whole integrand is u^3 du.
questions.question: AQ5(iv). Evaluate: integral of (x + 1)(x + log x)^3/x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = x + log x; then du = (1 + 1/x) dx = (x + 1)/x dx. The integral = integral u^3 du = u^4/4 + c = (x + log x)^4/4 + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply top and bottom by e^x: the integrand becomes e^x/(1 + e^x), whose derivative is the denominator.
questions.question: AQ5(v). Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + e^(-x)).
questions.solution: 1/(1 + e^(-x)) = e^x/(1 + e^x). With u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx, the integral = log(1 + e^x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608). Equivalent form: x - log(1 + e^x) + c.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: The denominator's derivative is 2(b - a) sin x cos x, so the answer is a logarithm divided by that constant.
questions.question: AQ5(vi). Evaluate: integral of sin x cos x dx/(a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x).
questions.solution: Let u = a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x. Then du = (-2a cos x sin x + 2b sin x cos x) dx = 2(b - a) sin x cos x dx, so sin x cos x dx = du/(2(b - a)). The integral = (1/(2(b - a))) log|a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(vi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: d(cos^2 x) = -sin 2x dx, so the minus sign of the substitution lands in front of the exponential.
questions.question: AQ5(vii). Evaluate: integral of e^(cos^2 x) sin 2x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = cos^2 x; du = -2 sin x cos x dx = -sin 2x dx. The integral = -integral e^u du = -e^u + c = -e^(cos^2 x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(vii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: d(e^(x^2)) = 2x e^(x^2) dx: the whole coefficient is the inner derivative, leaving sec^2 u du.
questions.question: AQ5(viii). Evaluate: integral of 2x e^(x^2) sec^2(e^(x^2)) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = e^(x^2); du = 2x e^(x^2) dx. The integral = integral sec^2 u du = tan u + c = tan(e^(x^2)) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(viii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = e^(sqrt x) with du = e^(sqrt x) dx/(2 sqrt x); then tan^2 u = sec^2 u - 1 gives two immediate integrals.
questions.question: AQ5(ix). Evaluate: integral of e^(sqrt x) tan^2(e^(sqrt x))/(2 sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = e^(sqrt x); du = e^(sqrt x) * (1/(2 sqrt x)) dx, exactly the factor present. The integral = integral tan^2 u du = integral (sec^2 u - 1) du = tan u - u + c = tan(e^(sqrt x)) - e^(sqrt x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(ix); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Write the denominator as tan x cos^2 x: the integrand becomes (tan x)^(-1/2) sec^2 x dx, i.e. u^(-1/2) du.
questions.question: AQ5(x). Evaluate: integral of sqrt(tan x)/(sin x cos x) dx.
questions.solution: sqrt(tan x)/(sin x cos x) = sqrt(tan x)/(tan x cos^2 x) = (tan x)^(-1/2) sec^2 x. With u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx: the integral = integral u^(-1/2) du = 2 sqrt u + c = 2 sqrt(tan x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(x); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle form: 1 + cos x = 2cos^2(x/2) and 1 + sin x = 1 + 2 sin(x/2)cos(x/2), giving sec^2(x/2)/2 plus tan(x/2).
questions.question: AQ5(xi). Evaluate: integral of (1 + sin x)/(1 + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos x = 2 cos^2(x/2) and sin x = 2 sin(x/2) cos(x/2), so the integrand = 1/(2cos^2(x/2)) + sin(x/2)/cos(x/2) = (1/2) sec^2(x/2) + tan(x/2). Integrate: tan(x/2) - 2 log|cos(x/2)| + c. Since 2 cos^2(x/2) = 1 + cos x, 2 log cos(x/2) = log(1 + cos x) - log 2, so the answer is tan(x/2) - log(1 + cos x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xi); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Split the numerator by the angle-addition formula: sin x = sin((x - alpha) + alpha) = sin(x-alpha)cos alpha + cos(x-alpha) sin alpha.
questions.question: AQ5(xii). Evaluate: integral of sin x dx/sin(x - alpha).
questions.solution: sin x = sin(x - alpha) cos alpha + cos(x - alpha) sin alpha, so sin x/sin(x - alpha) = cos alpha + sin alpha * cot(x - alpha). The integral is therefore x cos alpha + sin alpha log|sin(x - alpha)| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by e^(-x)/e^(-x): the integrand becomes e^(-x)/(1 + e^(-x)), whose denominator has derivative -e^(-x).
questions.question: AQ5(xiii). Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + e^x).
questions.solution: 1/(1 + e^x) = e^(-x)/(e^(-x) + 1). With u = 1 + e^(-x), du = -e^(-x) dx, the integral = -log(1 + e^(-x)) + c. Boxed (printed key p608). This equals x - log(1 + e^x) + c, the same family as AQ5(v).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ5(xiii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: 1 + cos x = 2cos^2(x/2), so the integrand is (x/2)sec^2(x/2) - one clean by-parts with v = 2tan(x/2).
questions.question: AQ6(i). Evaluate: integral of x/(1 + cos x) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos x = 2 cos^2(x/2), so the integral = (1/2) integral x sec^2(x/2) dx. By parts with u = x, dv = sec^2(x/2)dx, v = 2 tan(x/2): (1/2)[2x tan(x/2) - 2 integral tan(x/2) dx] = x tan(x/2) - integral tan(x/2) dx = x tan(x/2) + 2 log|cos(x/2)| + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(i); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Differentiate the answer to see the structure: log(1 - cos x) supplies sin x/(1 - cos x) and x cot(x/2) supplies the -x/(1 - cos x) part.
questions.question: AQ6(ii). Evaluate: integral of (sin x - x)/(1 - cos x) dx.
questions.solution: Write the integrand as sin x/(1 - cos x) - x/(1 - cos x). The first part integrates to log(1 - cos x) because d(1 - cos x) = sin x dx. For the second, 1 - cos x = 2 sin^2(x/2), so x/(1 - cos x) = (x/2) cosec^2(x/2); by parts with u = x, dv = (1/2)cosec^2(x/2)dx, v = -cot(x/2): integral = -x cot(x/2) + integral cot(x/2) dx = -x cot(x/2) + 2 log|sin(x/2)|. Subtracting gives log(1 - cos x) + x cot(x/2) - 2 log sin(x/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(ii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute u = sqrt x (dx = 2u du) to get 2 integral u e^u du, then one by-parts.
questions.question: AQ6(iii). Evaluate: integral of e^(sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du. The integral = 2 integral u e^u du = 2(u e^u - e^u) + c = 2 e^(sqrt x)(sqrt x - 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(iii); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: Recognise a product-rule derivative: d(x/log x) = 1/log x - x*(1/x)/(log x)^2 = 1/log x - 1/(log x)^2.
questions.question: AQ6(iv). Evaluate: integral of {1/log x - 1/(log x)^2} dx.
questions.solution: Observe that d/dx [x/log x] = 1/log x - x(1/x)/(log x)^2 = 1/log x - 1/(log x)^2, which is exactly the integrand. Hence the integral = x/log x + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(iv); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: u = sqrt x gives 2 integral u sin u du, and that by-parts is the standard -u cos u + sin u.
questions.question: AQ6(v). Evaluate: integral of sin(sqrt x) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du. The integral = 2 integral u sin u du = 2(-u cos u + sin u) + c = 2(sin sqrt x - sqrt x cos sqrt x) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS AQ6(v); book p605-607 = PDF p632-634; key book p607-608 = PDF p634-635

questions.knowledgeNote: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, so u = sin x turns it into 2 integral u e^u du.
questions.question: AQ6(vi). Evaluate: integral of e^(sin x) sin 2x dx.
questions.solution: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x. With u = sin x, du = cos x dx: the integral = 2 integral u e^u du = 2 e^u(u - 1) + c = 2 e^(sin x)(sin x - 1) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: Two rounds of by parts: x^2 -> 2x -> 2, giving e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2).
questions.question: AQ6(vii). Evaluate: integral of x^2 e^x dx. (HSEB 2054).
questions.solution: By parts twice: integral x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - 2 integral x e^x dx, and integral x e^x dx = x e^x - e^x. Hence integral x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - 2x e^x + 2 e^x + c = e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: First linearise sin^3 x = (3 sin x - sin 3x)/4, then do two by-parts integrals of x times a sine.
questions.question: AQ6(viii). Evaluate: integral of x sin^3 x dx.
questions.solution: sin^3 x = (3 sin x - sin 3x)/4, so the integral = (3/4) integral x sin x dx - (1/4) integral x sin 3x dx. Using integral x sin(ax) dx = sin(ax)/a^2 - x cos(ax)/a: the first is (-x cos x + sin x) and the second is (-x cos 3x/3 + sin 3x/9). Therefore the answer is -(3/4)x cos x + (3/4) sin x + (1/12)x cos 3x - (1/36) sin 3x + c. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: Both integrals over a quarter period are pi/4, so the answer is (a + b)pi/4 - no dependence on the mixture.
questions.question: AQ7(i). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of (a cos^2 x + b sin^2 x) dx.
questions.solution: integral 0 to pi/2 of cos^2 x dx = pi/4 and integral 0 to pi/2 of sin^2 x dx = pi/4 (both are half the interval, by symmetry of the linearised integrands). Hence the value = a(pi/4) + b(pi/4) = (1/4)(a + b)pi. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor sqrt x out of the denominator and substitute u = sqrt x, which turns the integrand into 2/(1 + u).
questions.question: AQ7(ii). Evaluate: integral from 0 to 1 of dx/(sqrt x + x).
questions.solution: sqrt x + x = sqrt x(1 + sqrt x). With u = sqrt x, dx = 2u du and the limits stay 0 and 1: the integral = integral from 0 to 1 of 2u du/[u(1 + u)] = 2 integral from 0 to 1 of du/(1 + u) = 2[log(1 + u)]_0^1 = 2 log 2. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: u = 1 + log x has du = dx/x and moves the limits to 1 and 3.
questions.question: AQ7(iii). Evaluate: integral from 1 to e^2 of dx/[x(1 + log x)^2].
questions.solution: Let u = 1 + log x, du = dx/x; when x = 1, u = 1; when x = e^2, u = 3. The integral = integral from 1 to 3 of u^(-2) du = [-1/u]_1^3 = -1/3 + 1 = 2/3. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^2 x cos^2 x = (1/4) sin^2 2x, then linearise again; the cosine term vanishes over the full quarter period.
questions.question: AQ7(iv). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin^2 x cos^2 x dx.
questions.solution: sin^2 x cos^2 x = (1/4) sin^2 2x = (1/8)(1 - cos 4x). Hence the integral = (1/8)[x - sin 4x/4]_0^{pi/2} = (1/8)(pi/2 - 0) = pi/16. Boxed (printed key p608).

questions.knowledgeNote: u = a^2 sin^2 + b^2 cos^2 has derivative 2(a^2 - b^2) sin cos, and the limits map to b^2 and a^2; the result factors as (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(3(a+b)).
questions.question: AQ7(v). Evaluate: integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin theta cos theta sqrt(a^2 sin^2 theta + b^2 cos^2 theta) d theta.
questions.solution: Let u = a^2 sin^2 theta + b^2 cos^2 theta; du = 2(a^2 - b^2) sin theta cos theta d theta, with u = b^2 at theta = 0 and u = a^2 at theta = pi/2. The integral = (1/(2(a^2 - b^2))) integral from b^2 to a^2 of u^(1/2) du = (1/(2(a^2 - b^2))) * (2/3)[u^(3/2)]_{b^2}^{a^2} = (a^3 - b^3)/(3(a^2 - b^2)) = (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(3(a + b)), using a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) and a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b). Boxed (printed key p608).
